comparison: Perfect agreement on mouse model data (C74-C80). Both accept the pristane-induced lupus findings showing ACK1/BRK inhibitors induce autoantibodies. Peer review notes model limitations ('failed to demonstrate the full picture of lupus') which aligns with OpenEval's cautious interpretation of C80 as hypothesis rather than definitive mechanism.

Perfect agreement on population genetics interpretation (C129-C131). Both accept that these variants represent rare Mendelian causes of SLE with limited population-level impact. Peer review describes this as 'a rare Mendelian cause of severe SLE.'

Strong agreement on ACK1 genetic variants (C36-C42). Peer review explicitly affirms identification of compound heterozygous variants without raising concerns. OpenEval finds genetic data internally consistent and well-supported. Peer result also covers BRK variants (C43-C53) which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

Strong agreement on BRK genetic variants (C43-C53). Peer review affirms identification of compound heterozygous variants in both ACK1 and BRK. OpenEval finds comprehensive genetic evidence is thorough and well-supported.

Strong agreement on biochemical characterization (C58-C66). Both accept in vitro kinase assays and auto-phosphorylation data. Peer review states no concerns raised about biochemical data. Peer result also covers iPSC functional data (C70-C73) which OpenEval addresses separately in R5.

Agreement on iPSC-derived macrophage functional validation (C67-C73). Peer review accepts biochemical characterization including patient cell data without challenge. OpenEval emphasizes this provides critical validation in disease-relevant cell type.

Agreement on iPSC generation and characterization (C67-C69). Peer review notes use of 'convincing...hiPSC-derived macrophages' and accepts cellular model system. OpenEval supports the iPSC approach as providing disease-relevant validation.

Strong agreement on MERTK signaling defects (C81-C82, C90-C93). Peer review implicitly accepts signaling defects by describing work as using 'convincing...experimental model.' OpenEval finds biochemical evidence linking variants to MERTK pathway loss of function is well-supported.

Agreement on MERTK-mediated signaling disruption (C27-C29). Peer review accepts that variants disrupt MERTK-mediated signaling without challenge. OpenEval identifies this as key mechanistic finding linking genetic variants to efferocytosis defects.

Agreement on transcriptional defects in anti-inflammatory response (C100-C102, C106-C107). Peer review explicitly states authors 'reported that ACK and BRK variants...impaired the MERTK-mediated anti-inflammatory response.' OpenEval finds RNA-seq and GSEA analysis appropriate and consistent.

Agreement on functional anti-inflammatory defects (C110-C115). Peer review accepts impaired anti-inflammatory response to apoptotic cells in iPSC-derived macrophages. OpenEval emphasizes ELISA data with isogenic controls directly test hallmark anti-inflammatory effect.

Agreement on key functional defects summary (C30-C31). Peer review accepts that variants impair MERTK-mediated anti-inflammatory response. OpenEval identifies these as critical validation of genetic findings in disease-relevant human cells.

Agreement on actin remodeling defects (C118-C121). Peer review accepts findings about modest engulfment defect without challenge. OpenEval finds TIRF microscopy data with quantification provides objective measurement of actin clearance defects.

Agreement on selective engulfment defects (C122-C123, C127). Peer review implicitly supports distinction between anti-inflammatory response and engulfment aspects. OpenEval emphasizes flow cytometry data showing selective defects in apoptotic cell uptake.

Agreement on engulfment defect characterization (C32). Peer review accepts data showing ACK1/BRK are more important for anti-inflammatory response than engulfment. OpenEval summarizes this as key functional defect in patient cells.

Agreement on specificity controls (C124-C126, C128). Peer review accepts specificity controls showing selective effects on apoptotic cells versus other cargos. OpenEval emphasizes these controls are critical for interpretation and strengthen mechanistic conclusions.

Agreement on selective phagocytic defect (C33). Peer review accepts specificity controls without challenge. OpenEval identifies this as important demonstration that defect is selective for apoptotic cells.

Agreement on mechanistic distinction (C132-C133, C136). Peer review implicitly supports distinction between anti-inflammatory signaling and engulfment. OpenEval finds conclusion well-supported by differential magnitude of effects in cytokine versus phagocytosis assays.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C137-C138). Peer review explicitly supports conclusions, calling work 'important study' that 'improves understanding of human SLE pathogenesis.' OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by convergence of multiple lines of evidence.

Agreement on study design and main genetic findings (C15-C17, with C16-C17 overlapping peer result). Peer review affirms identification of variants. OpenEval finds these central to paper's contribution and well-supported by detailed genetic analysis.

Agreement on mechanistic hypotheses (C35, C80, C97, with C80 overlapping peer result). Both appropriately treat these as hypotheses. Peer review notes model limitations, OpenEval emphasizes claims are stated as possibilities ('may contribute') rather than proven mechanisms.

OpenEval evaluates structural and computational evidence for variant pathogenicity (C54-C57) including domain mapping, 3D structures, conservation, and prediction algorithms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific bioinformatic analyses.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims about SLE (C1-C14) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer review does not separately evaluate these contextual claims, focusing instead on novel findings.

OpenEval evaluates extensive literature-based mechanistic context claims (C18, C22-C26, C83-C89, C94-C96, C98-C99, C103-C105, C108-C109, C116-C117, C134-C135) as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer review does not separately evaluate these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates mouse model findings about requirement for additional factors (C19-C21), noting ACK1/BRK deficiency requires genetic background and environmental triggers. Peer review addresses mouse models but does not separately evaluate these specific negative/positive findings about disease manifestation requirements.
